# System Window — deploy guide

_Last updated: 2026-08-26 (streak commit)_

## Why Vercel
Free tier is genuinely free (no card required), it auto-detects Vite projects
with zero config, gives you HTTPS on a `*.vercel.app` subdomain immediately
(HTTPS is required for the app to be installable as a PWA), and every time
you push new code it redeploys automatically.

## One-time setup

1. **Create a GitHub account** if you don't have one (free): https://github.com/signup
2. **Create a new repository** (e.g. `system-window`), then upload this
   entire folder to it. Easiest way if you're not familiar with git:
   on the repo page, click "uploading an existing file" and drag in
   everything in this folder (keep the folder structure — `src/`, `public/`,
   `index.html`, `package.json`, `vite.config.js`).
3. **Create a Vercel account** (free): https://vercel.com/signup — sign up
   with your GitHub account, it's the fastest path.
4. On the Vercel dashboard, click **Add New → Project**, choose the
   `system-window` repo you just created. Vercel will detect it's a Vite
   app automatically — you don't need to change any settings. Click **Deploy**.
5. After ~1 minute you'll get a live URL like `system-window-yourname.vercel.app`.
   That's it — it's live, free, and on the public internet with HTTPS.

## Setting up login + cloud-saved progress (Firebase)

The app is now gated behind Google Sign-In, and your progress is saved to
a private cloud database instead of just the phone's local storage — so
it follows your account, and only the email(s) you allow can get in.

### 1. Create the Firebase project (free, no card)
1. Go to https://console.firebase.google.com and sign in with your Google account.
2. Click **Add project**, name it (e.g. `system-window`), skip Google
   Analytics if asked (not needed).

### 2. Turn on Google Sign-In
1. In the left sidebar: **Build → Authentication → Get started**.
2. Under **Sign-in method**, enable **Google**, pick a support email, Save.

### 3. Create the database
1. Left sidebar: **Build → Firestore Database → Create database**.
2. Choose **production mode**, pick any region, Create.

### 4. Create the allowlist (do this BEFORE publishing rules)
The list of who's allowed in lives as data, not code — so adding someone
later is just editing this document, no redeploy needed.
1. Go to the **Data** tab → **Start collection**.
2. Collection ID: `config`. Document ID: `allowlist`.
3. Add a field: name `emails`, type **array**. Add one string entry per
   person you want to let in — your own Gmail address at minimum, in
   lowercase. Save.

### 5. Publish the security rules
1. Go to the **Rules** tab, delete what's there, and paste in the entire
   contents of `firestore.rules` from this project exactly as-is (nothing
   to edit in this file — the email list lives in the `config/allowlist`
   document from step 4, not here). Click **Publish**.

### 6. Get your web app config
1. Click the gear icon → **Project settings** → scroll to **Your apps** →
   click the `</>` (web) icon → register an app (any nickname).
2. It'll show a `firebaseConfig` object with values like `apiKey`,
   `authDomain`, etc. — you'll need these next.

### 7. Set the environment variables
- **Locally:** copy `.env.local.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the
  values from step 6.
- **On Vercel:** Project → Settings → Environment Variables → add each
  `VITE_FIREBASE_...` key from `.env.local.example` with its value from
  step 6. Redeploy after saving.

### 8. Authorize your deployed domain
Firebase only allows sign-in popups from domains you've approved:
**Authentication → Settings → Authorized domains → Add domain**, and add
your `*.vercel.app` URL.

Once all eight steps are done, push to GitHub, let Vercel redeploy, and
opening the app will show a "Sign in with Google" screen. Only accounts
listed in the `config/allowlist` Firestore document get past it — everyone
else sees "Access denied."

**Adding someone later:** Firestore Database → Data tab → `config` →
`allowlist` → edit the `emails` array → add their address → Save. Takes
effect immediately, no code change, no redeploy.

## Installing it on your phone

1. Open the Vercel URL in **Safari** (iPhone) or **Chrome** (Android).
2. **iPhone:** tap the Share icon → "Add to Home Screen".
   **Android/Chrome:** tap the ⋮ menu → "Install app" (or "Add to Home Screen").
3. It now sits on your home screen with its own icon, opens full-screen with
   no browser bar, and works offline once you've opened it at least once.

## Updating it later without losing data

- Your data (profile, checklists, achievements, currency, everything) now
  lives in Firestore under your account (`users/{your-uid}/...`) — not in
  the app's code or the deploy itself, and not tied to one specific phone.
- Push new code to the same GitHub repo → Vercel redeploys automatically →
  your saved data is untouched, because it was never part of the
  deployment in the first place. Sign in with the same Google account on
  any device and your progress is right there.
- The Settings window's export/import is still worth using occasionally
  as an extra backup, independent of the cloud database.

## Local testing (optional, needs Node.js installed)

```bash
npm install
npm run dev      # opens a local dev server
npm run build    # builds the production files Vercel would deploy
```
